errors.english: the Jewel among Men born for the sake of the world's happiness
errors.why: bde bar 'gro ba renders Sugata (Skt. sugate): a Sugata, a jewel of a man, is born; it is an epithet of the Buddha, not 'for the world's happiness'.

errors.why: The Tibetan simply breaks off at 'the city'; 'ends mid-sentence' is an unmarked editorial remark printed as if part of the translation.

Karmavācanā technicalities (jñapti, jñaptidvitīya, jñapticaturtha, sīmā markers, Upāli citation) are correctly handled; a few literal renderings ('perfectly/nearly abiding') remain opaque but are not clearly wrong.
Accurate rendering of the discussion of contradictory reasons and of the words 'oneself' and 'wished' in the definition of the thesis.

errors.english: Therefore, time is indeed something to be grasped by the valid means of direct inference.
errors.why: mngon sum gyi tshad ma is perception; the opponent concludes that time is grasped by perception alone.

errors.english: Thus, since slowness and other qualities would not be otherwise logical, the intention is that time is not something to be inferred.
errors.why: The point is that time cannot be inferred on the ground that slowness etc. would otherwise be impossible (arthāpatti), since slowness is explained without time; the English makes the impossibility the reason for the denial, inverting the argument.

errors.english: Furthermore, because others are otherwise illogical...
errors.why: gzhan dag are other opponents who argue that time is inferred from otherwise-impossibility; 'others' is the agent, not what is illogical.

note: Commentary on the refutation of time as a perceptible or inferable entity; perception is mistranslated as inference at a key conclusion and the arthāpatti argument is garbled.
Faithful word-by-word gloss commentary on the tigress episode; glosses and the cited verse are correctly rendered.

errors.english: Likewise, when birth occurs through the linking of another moment of similar kind, this is purely a negation.
errors.why: Destruction is merely the negation of the arising, through linkage, of a further moment of similar kind; the English makes the arising itself the negation.

fix.find: Likewise, when birth occurs through the linking of another moment of similar kind, this is purely a negation.
fix.replace: Likewise, it is purely the negation of the arising, through linkage, of another moment of similar kind.

note: Good rendering of the Tattvasaṃgraha-pañjikā on the two kinds of destruction and the contradiction of non-coexistence, with one misconstrued clause.

errors.english: Actions differentiated by virtue and so forth are likewise of two kinds.
errors.why: This sentence is the commentary's prose lead-in; only the two lines 'drang srong mchog gi las rnams ni / sems pa dang ni bsam par gsungs' are the root verse (MMK 17.2ab), but the English sets the prose as a verse line.

note: Accurate treatment of cetanā and cetayitvā karma and the epithet paramarṣi; one prose sentence is merged into the root verse.

errors.english: When the mind engages with an entity [note: original: "vastu"], it produces an incompatible cause
errors.why: It is the cognition of non-entity that, by producing an incompatible cause in the form of a vāsanā, cuts off the continuum of the entity-cognition; the English makes the entity-cognition produce the incompatible cause.

note: Generally sound rendering of the argument on the contradiction of entity and non-entity conceptions; one agent confusion at the opening.
